rationale: PINS the evidence-verified imported-binding claim (Lead contract 2026-10-18). Two halves: (1) EVERY imports edge publishes the LOCAL names it binds in metadata.importedBindings (default import, named import incl. alias, namespace local, require() destructure/bare binding) — this is the EVIDENCE the arbiter verifies; (2) an edge whose TARGET IS that binding carries metadata.importedBinding = {specifier, binding} and the target stays BARE — no BINDING_SEP spelling, because this claim is evidence-verified rather than spelling-verified (unlike the local-binding class). The imports rows are pinnable here (arrays compare by sorted JSON); the claim OBJECT is machine-checked by the gate/arbiter control arms, and this fixture pins the half that matters for regressions: the local names on every import row and the BARE spelling of every claimed target. NEGATIVES: a name the FILE declares (localOnly) has no import evidence -> bare, unclaimed; a namespace MEMBER access (ns.foo -> target foo) is a member, not the binding; a DYNAMIC specifier (require(moduleName)) has no literal evidence -> bare, unclaimed. The imports rows ALSO pin meta.module - the arbiter's evidence KEY: the first arbiter smoke refuted six importedBinding claims because the require()/import() evidence rows carried no module field (all six were require-bound: fs, path, an absolute pg path, ../utils/logger, ../../services/...); the analyzer now publishes it on every imports row, from stringContent() of the SAME written argument the claim specifier comes from, so the two spellings cannot drift.
